evidence.quote: We revisited classical software productivity analyses on ISBSG and Finnish datasets. The differences of critical factors between the propensity score and the linear regression were investigated.
The procedure of PSM is three-folds: 1) calculation of propensity score, 2) matching data points based on the score, and 3) calculation of average treatment effect (ATE).
Included projects were collected from software development companies in 20 countries. The dataset has 3026 projects and 99 variables.
the number of data points was 610 in the analysis
The dataset has 407 projects and 45 variables. We deleted projects whose software size, duration, and effort were zero. As a result, 400 projects remained.
The productivity was defined as a ratio of FP divided by summary work effort, and follows traditional definition [15].
This section focused on the influence of required quality of software to productivity.
